lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The ink remained wet beneath the library's colorless light. It had pooled slightly at the hooks of the letters, as if the Ledger had written in haste, though nothing else in the chamber suggested urgency. The jars stood motionless on their shelves. The tiny figures within them continued their unfinished gestures, repeating movements too small to make a sound. Even the walls had quieted. NEEN-soon could hear Zeek's breathing beside her and, beneath it, the faint settling of the copper figurine in her fist whenever her grip shifted.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek had not moved since the sentence appeared. His left hand remained fixed to the calcified key resting against the Ledger, the distinction between his skin and the pale mineral around it nearly gone. The grayness that had begun at his fingertips now crossed the back of his hand in branching lines, climbed his wrist, and vanished beneath his sleeve. More of it showed above his collar. It followed the veins of his throat like writing worked beneath the skin by someone who had no patience for spacing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon forced herself to look away from him and examine the desk.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Ledger occupied most of its surface. Blank pages waited beyond the command, their edges clean despite the dust coating everything around them. The quill lay to the right, set parallel to the book's spine with the care of an instrument prepared before a procedure. Its shaft had the same chalk-white texture as the key fused to Zeek's hand. No inkpot stood nearby. There were no stains on the desk, no discarded nibs, no scraped practice marks. Yet the final sentence shone as if written seconds ago.

A shelf she remembered against the eastern wall stood several paces nearer, though no track marked its passage through the dust.

lines.text: The distance of one pace felt like betrayal. The second felt worse. By the third, the passage had begun to contract behind her, shelves drawing inward without moving. She turned and ran before the opening could decide it had never existed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The corridor changed beneath each footfall. Numbers carved beside the shelves vanished as she passed. One arch narrowed until her shoulder struck stone that had not been there when she entered it. A row of jars appeared ahead, blocking the passage, and for a sickening moment she saw the father's label among them—SUBJECT 001, the dash still waiting—before every vessel darkened and the row became a wall.

lines.text: NEEN-soon swerved through an opening to her right.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind her, the scratch of the quill continued. It followed through walls and turns, sometimes close enough to seem beside her ear, sometimes buried so deep beneath the stone that it might have been the City itself writing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A staircase rose beneath her without warning. She stumbled onto the first step, caught herself against the wall, and climbed as the lower steps flattened behind her. Halfway up, the staircase angled sideways. NEEN-soon braced both hands against the narrowing stone and forced herself through. BAH-lahg's axe head struck the wall with every movement. En-KHEH-doo's figurine cut into her palm inside her pocket.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At the top, daylight filled a doorway no larger than a burial niche.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon threw herself through as the stone narrowed against her shoulders. Heat struck her face. Sand scraped beneath her palms when she landed. She rolled, came to her knees, and dragged one boot free an instant before the threshold sealed behind it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For several breaths she could do nothing but kneel in the sand and pull air into lungs that had forgotten how open space felt. The sky stretched above her without pillars or ceiling. Sunlight hurt her eyes. Every exposed inch of skin seemed to tighten beneath the heat.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind her, a narrow doorway remained cut into the rock.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No darkness showed within it. Only a pale gray surface, deeper than shadow, shifting as though pages turned somewhere beyond sight.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She took one step toward it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scratch of the quill had stopped.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her body turned before she permitted it. She caught herself with one hand against the rock and stared at the sand near her feet.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.note: Ninsun remembering Zik's last instruction. Exhausted irritation, not ceremony.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's last instruction had been neither noble nor ceremonial. He had spoken it with the same exhausted irritation he used when she interfered with a measurement or refused to admit a corridor was unstable. The familiarity of it made obedience harder.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She waited for his voice, for a hand against the stone, for the blunt scrape of his boots crossing the threshold. The wind passed between the rocks and carried nothing with it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The doorway narrowed by the width of a finger.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon pressed her forehead against the sun-warmed stone beside it.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The gray surface inside the opening rippled once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not a fist. Not a body. A single dull vibration traveled through the rock and into her hand, followed by the faint sound of a page being turned.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The edges met without grinding. The seam thinned, disappeared, and left an unbroken face of stone beneath her palm.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon remained there until the rock grew too hot to touch. When she finally lowered her hand, En-KHEH-doo's copper figurine had marked her palm, and BAH-lahg's axe head pulled heavily at her belt. She did not search the stone for another entrance. She did not call Zeek's name again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She turned toward the desert with the City sealed behind her and began walking before it could decide to remember the door.
